stem: Per Rule 040102, from what date is an officer's emolument on first appointment generally paid?

options.A: From the date the officer is placed on the IPPIS platform
options.B: From the date of the appointment letter
options.C: From the first day of the following calendar month
options.D: From the date the officer assumes duty

explanation: Rule 040102: on first appointment, emolument shall as a general rule be paid as from the date of assumption of duty.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 040102, within how long of assuming duty must an officer be placed on the IPPIS platform?
explanation: Rule 040102: all officers shall be placed on the IPPIS platform within two months of assumption of duty.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Under Rule 040103, from what date does a staff member transferred from another scheduled service become eligible for the emolument attached to their new office?

options.A: From the date the transfer decision is signed
options.B: From the date they assume duty in the new office
options.C: From the date of their original first appointment to the Public Service
options.D: From the first day of the following incremental year

explanation: Rule 040103: a staff on transfer is eligible for the emolument attached to the new office with effect from the date they assume duty.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Under Rule 040104(i), where an officer is promoted to a grade level that does not overlap their old grade level, where are they placed on the new salary scale?

options.A: At the maximum point of the new salary grade level
options.B: At the minimum point of the new salary grade level
options.C: At the same numeric point they held on the old grade level
options.D: At the midpoint between the old and new grade levels

explanation: Rule 040104(i): if the officer is promoted to a grade level that does not overlap the old one, they are placed at the minimum point of the new salary grade level.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Under Rule 040104(ii), if an officer's former emolument is already higher than the minimum point of their new grade level, where are they placed?

options.A: At exactly their former emolument, frozen until the next incremental date
options.B: At the maximum point of the new grade level
options.C: At the next point higher than their former emolument, after accounting for the increment they would otherwise have earned
options.D: At the minimum point of the new grade level regardless

explanation: Rule 040104(ii): they are placed on the next point higher than their former emolument, taking into consideration the increment they would have earned had they not been promoted.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Under Rule 040104(iii), by when must promotion arrears be paid?

options.A: Within the year the promotion is effected
options.B: Within the same month the promotion is effected
options.C: Whenever the officer's next incremental date falls
options.D: Within two years of the promotion

explanation: Rule 040104(iii): payment of promotion arrears shall be made within the year promotion is effected.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: How does Rule 040201 define an increment?

options.A: A predetermined amount added to an officer's annual emolument every calendar year
options.B: A one-time bonus payable only on promotion
options.C: A discretionary amount set entirely by the officer's Permanent Secretary
options.D: A percentage of the officer's basic salary paid quarterly

explanation: Rule 040201: increment is a predetermined amount added to the annual emolument of an officer every calendar year.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 040202, which of these is explicitly listed as a ground on which an officer's increment would normally NOT be granted?

options.A: The officer has fewer than three years of total service
options.B: The officer recently transferred from another Ministry
options.C: The officer is on interdiction or suspension
options.D: The officer is on approved annual leave

explanation: Rule 040202: an increment is normally granted unless the officer is on interdiction/suspension, has a pending disciplinary action, or is held back on account of poor performance.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 040203, an officer's incremental date is fixed as 1st January of the year following at least how many months of service or promotion?
explanation: Rule 040203: the incremental date is 1st January of the year following at least six months of service or promotion.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 040205, what is the shortest period for which an increment may initially be deferred?
explanation: Rule 040205: the deferment period must be fixed at the time of deferment, and must not be less than three months nor more than six months.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 040205, what is the longest period for which an increment may be deferred, even after extension?
explanation: Rule 040205: if less than six months in the first instance, the deferment may be increased, but only up to six months.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Under Rule 040205, when a deferred increment is eventually granted, from what point does it become effective?

options.A: From the start of the following calendar year
options.B: Immediately on the date the decision to grant it is made
options.C: The day following the expiration of the deferment period
options.D: Retroactively, from the original incremental date

explanation: Rule 040205: if a deferred increment is eventually granted, it does not become effective until the day following the expiration of the specific period of deferment.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Under Rule 040205, if a deferred increment is still not granted by the time six months have passed from when it was originally due, what must happen?

options.B: The deferment period is automatically extended by another six months
options.C: The matter is referred directly to the Federal Civil Service Commission for a fresh decision
options.D: It must be automatically granted in full

explanation: Rule 040205: if a deferred increment is not granted at or before the expiration of six months from the date it was originally due, it must be withheld.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Under Rule 040206, what happens to an officer whose increment is withheld?

options.A: They lose all future eligibility for increments permanently
options.B: They become ineligible for that increment until their next incremental date
options.C: Their emolument is reduced below its pre-increment level
options.D: They are automatically placed under disciplinary investigation

explanation: Rule 040206: an officer's increment is withheld when it is decided not to grant it, and they cease to be eligible for it until their next incremental date.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 040204, which penalty is described as more serious: deferring an increment, or withholding it?

options.C: They are treated as equally serious under the Rules
options.D: Neither is treated as a penalty

explanation: Rule 040204: the Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office bears in mind that to withhold an increment is a more serious penalty than to defer it.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Under Rule 040207, can a deferred or withheld increment be restored with retrospective effect because the officer's service later improves?

options.A: Yes, provided the officer formally appeals within thirty days
options.B: No -- it cannot be restored retrospectively for that reason
options.C: Yes, but only with the Federal Civil Service Commission's prior written approval
options.D: Yes, automatically, once service improves for six consecutive months

explanation: Rule 040207: an increment deferred or withheld cannot be restored with retrospective effect in consequence of improved service during a later increment-earning period.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Under Rule 040209, which body may grant special increments to mitigate the lasting effects of a previously withheld increment?

options.C: The Office of the Accountant General of the Federation
options.D: The officer's own Permanent Secretary, acting alone

explanation: Rule 040209: the Federal Civil Service Commission may at a subsequent incremental date grant one or more special increments to mitigate the lasting effects of a withheld increment.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 040210, within how long must a decision to defer or withhold an increment, or stop a salary, be communicated to the relevant offices and the officer concerned?
explanation: Rule 040210: such decisions shall be communicated within two weeks to the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation, the Office of the Auditor-General for the Federation, the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, and the officer concerned.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 040208, when a decision is made to restore a previously withheld or deferred increment, what must the Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office do?

options.A: Refer the decision to the Federal Civil Service Commission for ratification before informing the officer
options.B: Publish the decision in the Federal Government Gazette
options.C: Wait until the officer's next incremental date to inform them
options.D: Immediately bring the decision to the notice of the officer

explanation: Rule 040208: immediately on deciding to restore an increment, the Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office should bring the decision to the notice of the officer.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.
